what_its_for: Eletriptan is used to treat migraine headaches in adults. It helps relieve the pain, nausea, and sensitivity to light and sound that come with a migraine. It is NOT used to prevent migraines before they start, and it does NOT treat other types of headaches like tension headaches or cluster headaches.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Take it as soon as you notice your migraine starting — the sooner you take it, the better it works. If your headache comes back after your first dose, you may take a second dose at least 2 hours after the first one. Do not take more than 80 mg in a 24-hour period. If your first dose does not help at all, do not take a second dose for the same migraine attack — contact your doctor instead.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 20 mg or 40 mg taken as a single tablet when the migraine begins. Your doctor may prescribe a higher dose of 40 mg if needed. The maximum dose for a single migraine attack is 80 mg (two 40 mg tablets, taken at least 2 hours apart). Do not take more than 80 mg within 24 hours. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: This medicine is taken only when you have a migraine — it is not taken on a regular daily schedule. There is no such thing as a 'missed dose.' Simply take it when your migraine begins. Never double up doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep the tablets in their original packaging, away from moisture, heat, and direct light. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking another dose of eletriptan or any other triptan (such as sumatriptan or rizatriptan) within 24 hours of this medicine. Avoid taking ergotamine-type medicines (such as ergotamine or dihydroergotamine) within 24 hours before or after eletriptan. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, as it can cause dizziness or drowsiness. Limit or avoid alcohol, as it can worsen headaches and increase dizziness. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as they may increase the level of this medicine in your body.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: chest pain, tightness, or pressure; shortness of breath; sudden severe headache unlike your usual migraine; weakness or numbness on one side of the body; slurred speech; vision changes; fast or irregular heartbeat; severe stomach pain; bloody diarrhea; signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; or very high blood pressure symptoms like severe headache, blurred vision, or confusion. Also call your doctor if your headaches are getting worse, are happening more often, or if this medicine stops working.
when_it_works: Eletriptan usually starts working within 30 minutes to 1 hour after taking it. Most people feel significant relief within 1 to 2 hours. It works best when taken at the first sign of a migraine headache. Results may vary from person to person.
special_populations: Older adults (over 65): This medicine has not been well studied in people over 65. Use with caution and only under close medical supervision. Children and teenagers: This medicine is not approved for use in patients under 18 years of age. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Small amounts of this medicine can pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while using eletriptan. Kidney or liver problems: If you have severe kidney or liver disease, your doctor may not prescribe this medicine or may adjust your dose carefully. Heart disease: This medicine should not be used if you have a history of heart disease, stroke, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or certain circulation problems. Always tell your doctor about all of your medical conditions before starting this medicine.
